rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (score 657.5, best so far). Mass at 0.4 kg and base_speed 1.1 lifted the oval finish rate to 0.90 and the s-bend to 1.00 (20 of 20). The slalom still finished 0 of 20, with progress 0.35, 1.8 line-loss events per run and max_error at the 0.06 m off-track limit. The slalom is the only track that fails, so the remaining work is sharp direction changes. Mass is already at its 0.4 kg minimum, so yaw inertia cannot be cut further. Off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 for any body width in range, so body width does not help. Iteration 2 showed that a larger sensor footprint or wider span hurt, so sensor geometry stays unchanged. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.10 to 0.95. Each base_speed cut from 1.25 to 1.15 to 1.10 raised slalom progress (0.17 to 0.30 to 0.35), and the slalom is limited by bend-entry speed. Oval finish time should rise from about 2.2 s to about 2.6 s, still under the 3 s limit. The s-bend should also gain margin. Everything else (mass, sensors, kp 6.0, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, last_direction line loss) is held fixed, so the speed effect can be attributed. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.45 with fewer line losses (below 1.5 per run), and oval and s-bend completion kept at or above 0.85. Hypotheses: (a) slalom excursions are entry-speed driven, so a further speed cut helps; (b) if oval completion falls below 0.8 or completion time exceeds 2.8 s, speed is the binding constraint and the speed cut has gone too far; (c) if slalom line_loss_events stay at 1.5 or more with the speed cut, the 12 mm sensors are missing the tape on tight bends and a sensor-span test (about +/-0.025 with 12 mm sensors, alone) is needed next. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on each track, plus control_effort for steering load.
